skills.name: Meta Ads MCP Connector
skills.description: Launchable account-scoped Meta Marketing API MCP server for bounded read-only insights with provider-verified identity and normalized diagnostics.

capabilities: Read bounded account, campaign, ad set, and ad-level Insights reports for explicitly allowed ad accounts.
Preserve provider reporting dates, account timezone, currency, and account attribution settings.
Live-verify the Meta application, token principal, permissions, expiry, business, and ad-account relationship.
auth_required: Meta access token plus application credentials with ads_read and business_management permissions
operational.approval_boundary: Insights GET requests only; business, account, fields, breakdowns, dates, pagination, timeout, and response-size limits are enforced before results are returned.

requires_setup: A Meta app and token with access to the configured business and sandbox or live ad account.
limitations: The connector exposes no campaign, budget, creative, audience, or account mutation operation.
Reports are limited to the packaged field and breakdown allowlists and the runtime owner's policy budgets.
Provider promotion requires a current clean-client smoke observation against an approved sandbox ad account.
usability.quickstart: Bind META_ADS_CREDENTIAL and META_ADS_POLICY, then register .mcp.json with Codex, Claude, or a generic MCP client.

authentication.credential_storage: Access tokens and application credentials remain in explicitly bound runtime environment sources and are never written into the package or readiness profile.
authentication.validation: The packaged driver uses Meta debug_token to verify application binding, principal, permissions, and lifetime, then verifies the selected ad account and owning business with that same token.
authentication.revocation: Invalidate the token in Meta Business Settings, remove the system user or app from the ad account, or rotate the Meta application secret.

skills.name: Ad Platform Executor Template
skills.description: MCP/tool template for a narrow DV360 and Google Ads executor that applies only approved, policy-checked campaign changes and records rollback evidence.

operational.connected_system: DV360 and Google Ads API execution layer
capabilities: Read current campaign or line item state before execution.
Validate approved change plans against policy and current platform state.
Apply bounded bid, budget, targeting, or status changes.
Verify post-write state and create rollback patches.
auth_required: Approval token for medium and high-risk writes
operational.approval_boundary: Applies only policy-approved bounded writes; high-risk changes require human approval and rollback evidence.

limitations: Reference executor contract only; no connected ad-platform implementation is packaged.
usability.quickstart: Review TOOL.md and implement the approved provider operations before registration.

skills.name: Conversion Event Reconciler
skills.description: Deterministically deduplicate browser and server conversion events and reconcile them with first-party business outcomes.

operational.connected_system: Local event fixtures or approved event export
capabilities: Deduplicate browser and server events by event name and event ID.
Preserve event provenance and flag conflicting values.
Reconcile conversions with first-party outcomes.
operational.approval_boundary: Reads supplied files and writes JSON to stdout; live event collection and platform uploads are out of scope.

limitations: A local deterministic script is packaged, but clean-client installation evidence is not yet recorded.
Live event collection and platform uploads are outside this package.

skills.name: OpenAI Ads Adapter Template
skills.description: Mock-first read-only adapter contract for OpenAI Ads accounts, campaigns, ads, insights, and product feeds.

operational.connected_system: OpenAI Ads API or local mock fixtures
capabilities: Read advertiser account metadata.
List campaigns and ads.
Retrieve campaign insights.
Validate product-feed records.
auth_required: Account-scoped OpenAI Ads API credential for live bindings
operational.approval_boundary: Read-only by design; future writes must use the existing policy-gated ad-platform executor.

limitations: Reference adapter contract only; no connected executable integration is packaged.
usability.quickstart: Use adtech/openai-ads-api-client for an executable mock or live read-only integration.

skills.name: OpenAI Ads API Client
skills.description: Dry-run-first client for mock or live read-only OpenAI Ads account, campaign, ad, and insights retrieval plus non-persisting Conversions API validation.

operational.connected_system: OpenAI Advertiser API and Ads Conversions API
capabilities: Read ad-account metadata.
List campaigns and ads.
Retrieve account, campaign, ad-group, or ad insights.
Validate conversion event batches locally or through validate-only server mode.
auth_required: OPENAI_ADS_API_KEY for live Advertiser API reads
OPENAI_ADS_PIXEL_ID and OPENAI_ADS_CONVERSIONS_API_KEY for remote conversion validation
operational.approval_boundary: Advertiser operations are GET-only; Conversions API requests always force validate_only true and cannot persist events.

requires_setup: For live reads, create an account-scoped Ads API key in OpenAI Ads Manager and configure the API base URL.
Keep API keys in environment variables outside agent context.
Write-capable operations require explicit approval outside this client.
limitations: Mock mode is local and read-only; live mode depends on an external API contract.
No published clean-client installation and live-readiness evidence is recorded yet.
Campaign, ad-group, ad, file, and feed mutations are intentionally excluded.
Conversion validation is dry-run only and does not persist events.
Automatic pagination, retries, and rate-limit backoff are not included in this first client.

skills.name: Agent Control Plane MCP Server
skills.description: Launchable local MCP authority for tenant-scoped policy decisions, exact human approvals, signed execution grants, ordered action records, restart recovery, and tamper-evident audit verification.

capabilities: Authenticate separate proposing-agent and executor identities and enforce tenant, capability, and provider-account scope.
Evaluate versioned policy outside the model and fail closed for unmatched actions.
Create exact approval requests and revalidate separately recorded human decisions.
Issue short-lived signed execution grants for downstream governed executors.
Revalidate current policy, approval, and executor scope while atomically claiming a grant at the external effect boundary.
Persist authenticated state, hashed receipt references, compacted recovery intents, idempotent action evidence, and a signed hash-chained audit log.
auth_required: Runtime-owned signed identity and independent signing keys
operational.approval_boundary: The MCP runtime can request approval but cannot install policy or decide approvals; administrator authority is available only through the separate operator entrypoint.

requires_setup: CONTROL_PLANE_STORE, signed identity, identity public key, audit key, and role-specific grant keys: issuer key pair for agents or public key only for executors.
A separately scoped administrator identity to install policy and record human approval decisions.
limitations: This server does not execute provider mutations; governed executors must verify grants at their own effect boundary.
The deterministic local store assumes one filesystem host and does not provide multi-host consensus.
Key rotation requires an explicit operator migration; silent fallback to an old or unknown key is not supported.
usability.quickstart: Create signed runtime and administrator identities, install a tenant policy with the operator CLI, then register .mcp.json.

authentication.credential_storage: Keys and signed identities remain in runtime-owned bindings. Executors reject the grant private key. The package stores no secrets, raw provider receipts, or provider credentials.
authentication.validation: The packaged driver verifies identity signature, role, tenant, scope, absolute expiry, store access, and the complete audit chain.
authentication.revocation: Remove or replace the runtime identity binding, rotate the identity key, activate a replacement policy, and stop any executor that trusts the old grant key.

skills.name: GA4 MCP Connector
skills.description: Launchable read-only GA4 Data API MCP server with bounded queries, property isolation, typed authentication, and normalized source metadata.

capabilities: Run bounded read-only reports for explicitly allowed GA4 properties.
Return normalized dimensions, metrics, pagination, and source freshness.
Live-verify bearer or service-account identity and property access.
auth_required: GA4 read-only OAuth credential with access to each allowed property
operational.approval_boundary: Read-only report retrieval only; property, field, date, pagination, timeout, and response-size bounds are enforced before results are returned.

requires_setup: GA4_CREDENTIAL runtime binding and GA4_ALLOWED_PROPERTY_IDS configuration.
Google Analytics Data API enabled with read access to each allowed property.
limitations: The connector does not expose GA4 administration or mutation endpoints.
Reports are limited to the packaged dimension and metric allowlists.
usability.quickstart: Configure GA4_CREDENTIAL, set GA4_ALLOWED_PROPERTY_IDS, then register .mcp.json with Codex, Claude, or a generic MCP client.

authentication.credential_storage: Credential JSON remains in an explicitly bound runtime environment source and is never written into the package or readiness profile.
authentication.validation: The packaged driver obtains an access token, verifies principal, scopes, and lifetime with Google's token-info endpoint, and uses that same token for a one-row read-only report against the selected property.
authentication.revocation: Revoke user grants in the Google Account or disable and rotate the service-account key in Google Cloud IAM.

skills.name: BigQuery MCP Query Runner
skills.description: Launchable read-only BigQuery MCP server with parameter binding, scope isolation, dry-run cost enforcement, bounded pagination, and typed diagnostics.

capabilities: Execute one parameterized read-only GoogleSQL query inside configured project, dataset, and location boundaries.
Dry-run every query and enforce provider-side maximum bytes billed before execution.
Return typed rows with bounded pagination, job identity, cost, cache, timeout, and source diagnostics.
auth_required: BigQuery OAuth credential with jobs.create and read access only to the configured datasets
operational.approval_boundary: Read-only queries only; project, billing project, dataset, location, SQL, parameter, byte, row, page, timeout, and response-size restrictions are enforced before results are returned.

requires_setup: BQ_CREDENTIAL and a BQ_POLICY envelope defining project, billing project, dataset, location, byte, row, timeout, and user-OAuth authority.
Google BigQuery API enabled with least-privilege access to the configured datasets.
limitations: Only SELECT or WITH GoogleSQL is accepted; scripts, DML, DDL, external queries, destinations, and unqualified external tables are rejected.
Workload identity uses Google STS plus service-account impersonation; direct unidentifiable federated tokens are not accepted for readiness evidence.
Provider verification requires a clean-client sandbox smoke observation; deterministic tests do not satisfy that release evidence gate.
usability.quickstart: Configure BQ_CREDENTIAL and BQ_POLICY, then register .mcp.json with Codex, Claude, or a generic MCP client.

authentication.credential_storage: Credential JSON and workload subject tokens remain in explicit runtime environment bindings and are never written into the package or readiness profile.
authentication.validation: The packaged driver verifies Google-attested identity, scope, lifetime, billing project, and a live dry-run plus one-row read-only query.
authentication.revocation: Revoke the user grant, disable or rotate the service-account key, or remove the workload identity binding in Google Cloud IAM.

apis: Google OAuth 2.0 and Security Token Service
